records.name: Kocaeli
records.summary:
A trans visitor in Kocaeli is subject to the same nationwide developments as anywhere else in the country. An October 2025 leaked omnibus draft would amend the penal code to imprison acts deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality (up to three years; up to four for same-sex ceremonies), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, and expose doctors to up to seven years in prison; national monitoring reports that 2025 hostility became explicit state policy — family-year directives from the head of state, a rights organisation closed, broadcast and arts-event censorship, three hate-motivated killings, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations and a 2.5-fold rise in detentions.

No statute, incident or court case specific to Kocaeli appears in the surviving sources for this record: the documents behind it are national-level and carry no provincial breakdown. The absence of province-specific documentation is not evidence of local tolerance — the nationwide framework and its 2025-26 escalation reach this province as any other.

records.name: Mardin
records.summary:
No province-specific measure, incident or institution concerning transgender visitors is documented here in this edition's audited sources: what governs a trans visitor is the national picture, and no local authority is recorded adding bans or enforcement programs of its own.

The national framework as documented: a draft judicial package leaked in October 2025 would carry terms up to three years for conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality, up to four for same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies, raise the gender-care age floor to twenty-five with mandatory infertility conditions, and remove civil-status recognition of gender change. The principal national LGBTI report (Feb 2026) called the previous year's hostility explicit state policy — 'Year of the Family' directives, censorship instructions, one organisation closed, three hate-motivated killings with trans victims over-represented, 89 ill-treatment cases mostly tied to breaking up gatherings, and 313 detentions.

Mardin lies in the country's south-east. Absence of provincial documentation describes the record, not a guarantee: national directives reach every province's institutions, and the assembly-ban and violence patterns were logged countrywide rather than per province.
